about: Falsifiable prefill predictions written BEFORE the prefill-chunk arms (real-comp1-ng-pf4096, -pf8192, -pf16384; arm definitions in our lab notes, not published) ran on odie. Written 2026-10-26T16:10Z; the arms run ~16:30Z-17:40Z. Model: the per-read prefill model of src/model.js prefillPass (data/prefill-physics.json). Do not edit the predicted numbers after the measurements land; add a 'measured' block beside them instead.
recipe: the build served on 2026-10-26, its no-gdn lever set (ledger rows odie-fnx-iq3xxs-2xb70-real-comp1-no-gdn-ss16-n16-1026, -r2, -r3; image 0de528f7): odie 2x Arc Pro B70, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, layer split 25, --batch 32 --batch-groups 2 --kv k8v4 --kv-resident 4096, MAX_CONTEXT 131072, STRATA_PREFILL_STREAM_CPU_SHARE=0.25, 16 real agents (the 16-agent recorded trace, 600 s warm-up, 300 s window as planned; the arms ran a 600 s window). The arms change only --prefill (chunk T).
equation: one read of T fresh tokens with chunk C: t(T) = ceil(T / C) x t_pass + T x m. t_pass = sum over the layer-split stages of nonresident expert bytes x (1 - cpu_share) / link + resident expert bytes / VRAM bandwidth (the expert pass each chunk pays). m = per-token compute, the one calibrated factor for strata (2 x active params / (eta x card int8 ops)). Server prefill P = sum T / sum t(T) over the run's reads. Useful agent output = 1 / (F / P + 1 / D) (strata reads stall decode, data/workload.json).

predictions.headline: a bigger chunk lifts server prefill only ~5-6 % (866 -> 913-922 tok/s) and 16-agent output ~2-3 % (83.4 -> 85.4-85.8), inside the 11 % replay noise: only reads over 2048 tokens (47 % of fresh tokens, p90 read 2.65k) pay fewer passes, and per-token compute m (0.757 ms) is 2.6x the pass per token (0.19 ms at 2048). Prefill on the served build is per-token compute-bound, not pass-bound. If the engine halves T to fit buffers, read the row of the halved chunk
predictions.falsified_if: measured P of any arm exceeds 1,000 tok/s (+15 %, outside noise): the pass cost is larger than the physics t_pass (e.g. per-chunk fixed work beyond the stream); measured P below 780 (-10 %): a bigger chunk adds cost the model does not carry (buffers, attention growth)

xestrata_022_one_b70.fit: least squares t = ceil(T / C) x t_pass + T x m over 1K-128K, C unknown for that build: C 16384 gives t_pass 0.74 s, m 0.359 ms (1K 926 vs 1,173, 4K 1,854 vs 1,639, 32K-128K 2,474 vs 2,464-2,513); C 8192 gives t_pass 0.81 s, m 0.305 ms. A 2048 chunk cannot fit the curve (m < 0). The one-card t_pass ~0.7-0.8 s against ~24 GB nonresident means an effective stream of ~30 GB/s or a CPU share near 0.5 (INFERRED)
xestrata_022_one_b70.lesson: xe0.2.2 on ONE B70 reads at ~0.36 ms a token where our served build (xe0.1.45-based, two cards in series) spends 0.757: per-token prefill compute, not the expert pass, is what the served build loses; an xe0.2.2-class per-token rate (0.36 ms) with its t_pass would predict P ~1.33k (chunk 2048) to ~1.46k (16384) at agent read sizes (INFERRED, other build; corrected 16:2xZ from an arithmetic slip "~1.7-1.9k")

vllm_cookbook_one_b70.fit: no stream term (all resident): t = t_pass + T x m. Two points (p512, p8192) give t_pass 0.034 s, m 0.128 ms; then p2048 predicts 6,924 (+3.7 %), p4096 7,340 (+2.0 %). The physics t_pass, every expert read once from VRAM (~18 GB int4 experts / 608 GB/s = 0.03 s, INFERRED size), matches the fitted 0.034 s. The 131K prompt (3,144 measured vs 7,800 predicted) is attention growth, a term this model leaves out. Recorded as a check of the pass physics and of what a fully resident B70 path reads per token (0.128 ms), not fitted into strata

post_hoc.label: POST-HOC (not in the predictions above; the run landed after this file): the same served-build recipe at ONE agent (replaying sessions from the same 16-session trace), 300 s warm-up, 600 s window

model.src: MODEL from the committed inputs, no refit: t_pass 0.3947 s, m 0.757 ms over this run's own 72 in-window reads (median 938, mean 2,187, max 51,337 fresh tokens; 121 chunks) = 167.0 s of prompt time for 157,499 fresh tokens. agent_tps_formula = 1 / (F / P + 1 / D) with F 8.09 and D 68.78 (the run's measured per-request decode median). agent_tps_with_gaps = 19,574 output tokens / (167.0 s prompt + 19,574 / 68.78 s decode + 122.3 s of replayed tool gaps)

measured.src: the run's replay result file (our lab notes, not published)

post_hoc.wall_time: 600 s window: server prompt 185.8 s (31.0 %) + server decode 298.8 s (49.8 %) = 80.8 %; the rest is the client-side gaps between one turn's end and the next send, 122.3 s summed over the 72 turns (median 0.71 s, max 20.7 s): the recorded tool gaps the replay plays back at gap_scale 1.0. One agent leaves the server idle in them; at 16 agents other agents' work fills them. The formula 1 / (F / P + 1 / D) has no gap term, so it over-predicts a lone agent by a third; with the gaps it is +4.5 %. The P miss (+10.7 %) is per-read work outside the pass model at this read mix: 75 conversation parks and 5 evictions with 1 restore in the window (server_delta), and longer reads (one 51k cold read) whose attention cost grows with depth

measured.src: the three arms' replay result files (our lab notes, not published; the batch's nonzero exit was a restore cpuset mismatch after the last arm, the data are good); ledger rows as named. P = fresh prompt tokens / server prompt time; F = fresh prompt tokens / output tokens (server totals, as the baseline's 4.88; the replay's client-side fresh_split F reads 4.77 / 3.99 / 3.94). err = predicted / measured - 1
measured.verdict: NOT FALSIFIED by the stated test (every arm's P inside 780-1000: 814 / 844 / 858). But the predicted gain did not show: P sits 1-6 % UNDER the 866 baseline instead of 5-6 % over it, so the model over-predicts P by 7.5-12.2 %, worst at the smallest chunk. Two parts held: P rises with the chunk (814 < 844 < 858, the predicted direction), and a bigger chunk is no big lever (all within the 11 % replay noise of the baseline). The 16-agent spread (77.8 / 89.7 / 87.6 against 85.4-85.8 predicted) follows F (5.41 / 4.86 / 4.52), not P
